Key Findings from Spend Concentration BUDGET BREAKDOWN
1. Extreme Spend Concentration 72.2% OF SPEND

Just 5% of order lines (239 drugs) account for 72.2% of our total drug spend ($61.35M hospital / $80.31B national). The top 10% (478 drugs) drive 84.9% ($72.17M hospital / $94.48B national).

2. High Concentration in 25 Core Medications TOP 25 FOCUS

The top 25 individual medications account for 32.2% ($27.33M hospital / $35.78B national) of the entire pharmacy budget, led by Humira(Cf) Pen, Ozempic, Biktarvy, Jardiance, and Trulicity.

3. Primary Clinical Spend Drivers INFUSIONS & DIABETES

Two areas drive most of this top tier: outpatient specialty infusions (like immunology and cancer treatments) and outpatient diabetes medications.

4. Targeted Review vs. Broad Cuts $3.2M OPPORTUNITY

Broad budget cuts across all generic supplies create extra work for nurses and doctors without moving our bottom line. Review efforts should focus on these top 25 lines.

Dual-Track Growth Engine: Manufacturer Price Hikes vs. Surging Patient Volume

National CMS RY2026 outpatient drug claims ($111.28B across 4,774 formulations) are normalized by a 0.0764% health system scaling factor to model a representative $85.0M regional hospital outpatient pharmacy budget.

1. Mature Specialty & Brand Price Inflation (Cohort A: 23.9%) Trulicity (+106.6% Unit Cost)  |  Xifaxan (74.1% Price-Led)
Unit price hikes drove over 55% of log spend growth on mature lines: Emflaza (66.0% price-led), Enbrel Sureclick (55.6%), Cosentyx (55.1%), and Vyvanse (+36.6% unit price vs. -14.8% unit volume).
2. Epidemiological Adoption & GLP-1 Surges (Cohort B: 76.1%) Ozempic (+928.7% Claims)  |  Jardiance (+256.7% Claims)
Ozempic spend surged +1,143% driven by prescription claims expanding from 322K to 3.31M fills (-25.5% unit cost mix shift); Dupixent Pen claims grew +13,082.5%.
3. Structural Growth Engine Distinction Dual-Track Log Decomposition  |  1,210 High-Growth Lines
Distinguishes manufacturer-driven price increases on mature brands from genuine clinical adoption surges, providing empirical grounds to update hospital order sets.
Key Evidence & Context COST DRIVER REVIEW
1. Dual-Track Structural Engine 23.9% PRICE VS 76.1% VOLUME

Across 3,765 complete longitudinal formulations (2020 to 2024), 1,210 formulations grew over 50% in gross spend, revealing two distinct structural growth engines rather than uniform expansion.

2. Cohort A: Manufacturer Price Creep MATURE SPECIALTY

Mature specialty formulations grew via price increases: Xifaxan (74.1% price-driven), Emflaza (66.0%), Trulicity (+106.6% unit price; 56.1% price-led), Enbrel (55.6%), Cosentyx (55.1%), and Vyvanse (+36.6% price vs. -14.8% volume).

3. Cohort B: Clinical Volume Surges NEW THERAPIES

Rapid clinical adoption drove claim volumes: Ozempic (+928.7% claim growth), Jardiance (+256.7% claims), and Dupixent Pen (+13,082.5% claims growth).

4. Actionable Clinical Governance P&T ORDER SETS

Overruns on mature lines were driven by manufacturer pricing rather than clinician overprescribing, giving P&T committees solid empirical footing to guide order sets.

Core Purchasing Inefficiencies 4 AUDIT FINDINGS
1. Unconverted Brand-Name Orders $1.1M OVERPAYMENT

The hospital still orders and dispenses brand-name medications when FDA-approved bioequivalent generics are available.

2. Wide Multi-Source Generic Price Spread 71.6% MEDIAN SPREAD

Across 1,358 multi-manufacturer molecules, the median interquartile price spread across competing labelers is 71.6%, with 65.8% exceeding the 35% variance benchmark (p < 0.001).

3. Ad-Hoc Bottle Selection $2.1M OVERPAYMENT

Without strict rules in purchasing, buyers often order whichever generic bottle is in stock, paying a markup for the packaging.

4. Supplier Standardization Opportunity SAME EFFICACY

Standardizing suppliers across these bioequivalent drugs lowers costs without changing clinical efficacy.

Financial Impact Projected Annual Recovery Across GPO Contract Tiering and Automatic Generic Substitution
05 / 07

Contract Tier Compliance and Automatic Substitution Recoup $3.2M Annually

Projected Annual Recovery Across Two Hospital Policy Adjustments

Projected Savings Waterfall Chart +$2.1M GPO TIERING + $1.1M AUTO SUBSTITUTION = $3.2M NET RECOVERY
Key Policy Levers STANDARDIZED POLICY
1. GPO Contract Tier Enforcement ($2.1M) +$2.1M / YR

Requiring buyers to order generics at our 25th-percentile contracted price stops wholesaler overpayment on routine stock.

2. Automatic Generic Substitution ($1.1M) +$1.1M / YR

Setting our order entry system to substitute bioequivalent generics automatically stops brand overpayment at discharge.

3. Supply Chain Reliability Safeguard 25TH-PCT CAP

Capping generic purchase prices at the 25th percentile of contracted suppliers keeps order volumes reliable and prevents supply shortages.

4. Clinical Safety Threshold Verified 1.8% DISRUPTION

Modeled changes affect 1.8% of chronic care regimens, staying safely below our 2.5% clinical safety threshold.
